answer: Each new identity locks an 80-credit bond in a vault, stamped with a ferrous seal bound to its key; the seal cannot be transferred or shared. To stay active, it must broadcast one signal each epoch, a signed record of its work filed in the vault ledger. A signal hash already on file is rejected, and a duplicate burns 40 credits. The kth fake still needs its own bond plus a 15-credit filing fee, so 1,000 fakes lock 80,000 credits and pay 15,000 per epoch. A rented signal fails because the vault checks the signer against the sealed key. An honest agent pays a bond once and files its own signal.
